subject: Mallory: intermittent stuttered requests, elevated 5xx and latency spike
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha@mallorycommerce.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 07:23:00 -0800
Subject: Mallory: intermittent stuttered requests, elevated 5xx and latency spike

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

We started seeing a pattern from ~06:45 PST this morning where a fraction (~7-12%) of our inference requests to your hosted endpoint either time out (504) or return 5xx spikes with token-generation stalls. Overall p50 is fine but our p95 and p99 latency jumped and the error rate rose from ~0.2% to 3.8%. It’s impacting user-facing checkout recommendations on our site.

We collected a short traceroute and logs (attached). Two observations on our side:
- Many TCP sessions show SYN retransmits and delayed ACKs before the request reaches your ingress.
- Our perimeter firewall vendor pushed a micro-update at ~00:30 UTC; ops is checking whether that coincides.

Can you confirm whether there were any routing changes, proxy failovers, or peering disruptions on Redwood’s side? This is elevated — our CTO has been looped in if this persists.

Requesting an initial ack and ETA for next update.

Thanks,
Aisha Malik
Head of Platform, Mallory Commerce
+aisha@mallorycommerce.com

Hi Aisha — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We’ve opened this as an urgent investigation.

Quick notes / immediate actions:
- I’ve added Vivek (Infra SRE) and Jonas (Edge) to triage the network path.
- Can you confirm whether the affected requests are only routed through your standard Peering / Proxy or if any legacy proxy routes may still be in use? (A single customer endpoint can sometimes be served via different egress paths.)
- We’ll capture server-side ingress histograms and gateway logs for the window you provided and share preliminary findings within 45 minutes.

Temporary mitigation options to consider (we can enact with your sign-off):
1) Reroute Mallory traffic to your dedicated capacity pool (bypass shared proxy layer).
2) Enable sticky routing to a single region to avoid cross-region peering oscillation.

I’ll follow up with Vivek’s notes.

—Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Mallory: intermittent stuttered requests, elevated 5xx and latency spike

Vanessa / Marissa / Aisha — initial triage below.

What we see from our edge:
- Around 06:40 PST there are short bursts of increased SYN retries and TCP session resets across a subset (~9%) of connections originating from Mallory’s announced prefixes. The resets correlate with CPU scheduling spikes on the proxy fleet that handles Mallory’s tenant routing.
- Edge telemetry suggests oscillation between two upstream paths: our standard shared proxy cluster and a cross-region peering path for Mallory’s eu-us failover (we normally use sticky routing; appears the TTL/probe feedback toggled at that window).
- No code deploys on our serving layer during the window.

Hypothesis: transient routing flaps + proxy instance reconnects caused TCP-level stalls and re-establishment that manifests as high latency and increased 5xx. There’s also evidence of asymmetric return path behavior (some return traffic follows a different NAT translation) which can expose SYN retry behavior.

Immediate asks for Aisha to help narrow root cause:
- Please confirm whether Mallory’s edge firewall applied the midnight micro-update across all gateways; if yes, can you share the vendor bulletin?
- We need the tcpdump/snippets you attached; our packet team will compare three-way handshake timing and TTLs.

Planned next steps from Redwood:
- Push detailed gateway logs (attached) and a stitch of the MIGRATION/ROUTE change history for the last 24 hours.
- If you’re open, we can temporarily switch Mallory to dedicated capacity and pin routing to one region within the hour — this will remove the proxy oscillation variable.

I’ll attach the edge log excerpts in the next message.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

- The SYN retry counts line up with your edge timestamps.
- A small fraction of our sessions show an unexpected TTL drop mid-path which suggests an inline device (proxy/NAT) rewriting TTLs or asymmetric routing.

We’re happy to accept the temporary mitigation to dedicated capacity while we continue to investigate on our side. Please trigger the route pin and confirm the cutover plan.

—Aisha Malik
Head of Platform, Mallory Commerce

Subject: RE: Mallory: intermittent stuttered requests, elevated 5xx and latency spike — mitigation and exec summary

Aisha / team — summary and next steps (for execs and Mallory leadership):

What happened (brief):
- Dec 18 06:40 PST: short-lived oscillation in Mallory’s egress path resulted in proxy instance reconnections and a subset of TCP sessions experiencing SYN retries / resets. This produced p95/p99 latency degradation and an increase in 5xx.
- Likely contributing factor: Mallory perimeter firewall micro-update at 00:30 UTC coincided with the timing and appears to have changed how some sessions tear down/establish (vendor bulletin attached).

Immediate mitigations enacted (completed):
- At 09:05 PST on Dec 18 we routed Mallory requests to a dedicated capacity pool and pinned routing to us-west-2 (this removed the cross-region peering oscillation).
- We applied a temporary gateway low-connection-retry policy to reduce session churn and increased connection timeouts for Mallory’s tenant by +250ms.

Impact and ask:
- We expect customer-facing latency and error-rate to return to baseline within the hour of the cutover. Mallory ops to confirm on your side.
- As this had customer-visible impact, I’m proposing a one-time service credit for the affected window and an operational runbook update to coordinate firewall vendor patching with us for future micro-updates.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Vivek: deep packet-level correlation and final RCA (due EOD Dec 20).
- Jonas: runbook update for peering/proxy failover coordination (due Dec 22).
- Vanessa / Marissa: coordinate credit approval and exec comms (we’ll draft a joint note).

Aisha — thank you for the quick signal and the artifacts. We’ll keep this thread updated.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
